newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis protest president's anti-gay remarks.
newsitem.headline: Israelis protest president's anti-gay remarks.

text.p: Hundreds of Israelis protested outside the Jerusalem home of President Ezer Weizman on Saturday a day after he said he took a negative view of "the phenomenon" of homosexuality.
Demonstrators held signs saying "Weizman is a Homophobic" and called for the president -- a former air force chief with a reputation for shooting from the hip -- to resign.
"I'm sure that the community was harmed and when violence is directed at individuals in the community...their blood will be on his hands," said one protester.
Weizman, 72, took aim at homosexuals during a speech to Israeli high school students in the northern city of Haifa and drew laughter from students by using high-pitched voice to punctuate his attack.

"(Homosexuality) is abnormal from a social point of view. I don't like it. What the public decides to do with (homosexuals), it will decide through laws. There are those who tolerate the phenomenon," he said in broadcast remarks.
"I know a lot of places where... I see someone and know exactly what he is." He said too much public attention has been focused on the gay community.

Weizman, whose presidential role in Israel is largely ceremonial and non-political, has drawn fire from women's groups for remarks they said were sexist and criticised for making political statements.
